content.title: Bucks vs. Suns: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/21/26)
content.text: The Milwaukee Bucks (28–41) face the Phoenix Suns (39–31) tonight at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix. The Suns enter the matchup on a four-game losing streak after navigating a difficult stretch against top teams from both conferences. On Thursday, they squandered a late double-digit lead, allowing the San Antonio Spurs to rally for a dramatic 101–100 victory capped by a buzzer-beating shot from Victor Wembanyama. Collin Gillespie led Phoenix with 24 points on 7-of-13 shooting, knocking down six three-pointers — his first 20-point performance after a five-game slump in which he averaged just 6.2 points per game. Devin Booker added 22 points and Jalen Green chipped in 17, though both struggled with efficiency, combining to shoot 15-of-41 from the field. Milwaukee, meanwhile, has dropped two straight and three of its last four games, surrendering at least 122 points in each of those losses. The Bucks’ defense has suffered in the absence of Giannis Antetokounmpo, and their offense has also faltered. They failed to reach 100 points in Thursday’s 128–96 loss to the Utah Jazz — a team that owns the league’s worst defensive record. Ryan Rollins led Milwaukee with just 15 points in that defeat, while Cam Thomas added 14. The Bucks shot only 41% from the field and managed just 19 points in the opening quarter. They now face a Phoenix team that, despite its recent struggles, typically offers a much stiffer defensive challenge. Expect Phoenix to bounce back behind the scoring punch of Booker and Green, whose shot creation should help the Suns regain offensive rhythm. Milwaukee’s defensive issues without Giannis could allow Phoenix to control the pace and secure a much-needed home win. Prediction: Phoenix Suns 119, Milwaukee Bucks 105 Injury Report Milwaukee Bucks Giannis Antetokounmpo — Out (Ankle) Gary Harris — GTD (Groin) Kevin Porter Jr. — GTD (Knee) Phoenix Suns Grayson Allen — Out (Knee) Royce O’Neale — Out (Knee) Dillon Brooks — Out (Hand) Mark Williams — Out (Foot) Amir Coffey — Out (Ankle) Haywood Highsmith — Out (Knee) How to Watch Bucks vs. Suns Tip-off for tonight’s Bucks-Suns game is set for 10:00 PM Eastern / 9:00 PM Central / 8:00 PM Mountain at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix. The game airs live locally on FanDuel Sports Network Wisconsin and Arizona’s Family. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month.
